items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: if p is prime, A -> B is a ring homomorphism with p = 0 in A and both A and B are perfect, then L_{B/A} is zero in D(B) (source lines 2035-2040). The proof observes that the Frobenius pair induces an isomorphism of the ring map with itself, hence an isomorphism of L_{B/A}, while the preceding lemma shows that the same map is homotopic to zero; an endomorphism that is both an isomorphism and null homotopic forces the object to vanish.
